item.title: Bainimarama, Qiliho questioned over alleged mutiny
item.description: Former Prime Minister Voreqe Bainimarama and former Police Commissioner Sitiveni Qiliho are being questioned at the Criminal Investigation Department Headquarters in Suva. Acting Police Commissioner Mesake Waqa confirms that the two are being questioned for allegedly mutiny. Stay with us for more.

item.title: Catholics turn out in numbers as Lent begins
item.description: Catholic churches across Fiji were filled today as members marked Ash Wednesday, signalling the start of the Lenten season. From morning to evening Mass, families, youths and the elderly received ashes on their foreheads in the shape of a cross – symbolising repentance and reflection as the 40-day journey towards Easter begins. item.title: Farming to be given national priority, similar to tourism
item.description: The agriculture sector is set to receive stronger national focus, as the government looks to elevate it to the same level of importance as Fiji’s tourism industry. Minister for Finance, Esrom Immanuel says the sector has proven its value during times of national hardship, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic when tourism came to a halt. […]

item.title: Nadi trader fined for non-delivery of goods
item.description: The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission has secured a conviction against a Nadi-based hardware and spare parts trader, resulting in over $8,000 in fines and restitution. item.title: Fiji cleared from the European Union tax blacklist
item.description: Fiji has officially been removed from the European Union list of non-cooperative jurisdictions for tax purposes. Fiji was first placed on the EU blacklist in March 2019 and was required to address issues related to tax transparency, fair taxation, and the implementation of Base Erosion Profit Shifting minimum standards.
